key_insight: RESCUE combines four specialized LLM agents with machine-learning and rule-based screening to identify potentially overlooked candidates for rare-disease genomic evaluation in EHRs.
clinical_relevance: The workflow could help institutions identify patients who may warrant exome or genome sequencing review, without replacing clinician assessment.
method: Ontology Agent maps clinical data to a four-tier genetic-evidence taxonomy.
Modeling Agent trains a positive-unlabeled XGBoost classifier; Screening Agent applies model-based and rule-based screening across the EHR.
Review Agent samples clinical notes to assess medical necessity and operational feasibility.
evidence_signal: In a retrospective pediatric-hospital evaluation, holdout AUC was 0.808 (n=12,591); among 175,842 screening-eligible patients, flagged patients were 7.4-fold more likely than controls to receive subsequent genomic assessments, and blinded chart review found 80% precision for appropriate sequencing candidates after accounting for prior testing.
watch_item: Single-hospital retrospective results require prospective, multi-site validation to establish generalizability, workflow burden, and effects on diagnosis.
paper_title: RESCUE: An end-to-end multi-agent LLM system for proactive rare-disease patient screening in the EHR
